milestones.objective: Improve the plan→execute cycle with branch management, phased execution, smarter debugging, and optional team coordination.

features.title: Branch creation from /cg-plan

features.title: Phased plan structure in /cg-plan

features.title: Phased execution in /cg-work
features.description: Support '/cg-work phase1' to execute a single phase and stop, enabling cross-session continuity. '/cg-work' without arguments runs all phases sequentially. Track completed phases in plan frontmatter so users can resume in new sessions.

features.title: Roadmap visualization agent + /cg-roadmap-view prompt
/cg-fixbug test-correctness assessment
features.description: Before fixing a bug, /cg-fixbug evaluates whether existing tests assert the intended behavior or merely codify the bug. Decides whether to fix the test, replace it, or write a new one — never blindly runs new code against old (possibly wrong) assertions.

features.title: GitHub Issues integration (optional, via gh CLI)
features.description: Opt-in feature for team coordination. If gh CLI is installed and user enables it: create GitHub issues from roadmap features, assign to team members, and link back to roadmap.json. features.title: PR verification pipeline (E2E smoke tests, parity checks, CONTRIBUTING.md)
features.description: Cross-platform E2E smoke tests in CI (cg-link/cg-unlink on fresh project dirs), automated cross-script parity checks (link.ps1 ↔ link.sh), conventional-commits lint, docs-staleness warning, CONTRIBUTING.md for contributors, and PR template with seven-dimension review checklist. Motivated by first external PR passing CI but failing on real macOS machine.

features.title: /cg-commit-push-pr — logical commit splitting, push, and PR creation
/cg-verify-pr — CI check verification and auto-fix dispatch
Goal-driven execution — plan-as-completion-contract with integrated validation
features.description: Transform the /cg-plan → /cg-work → /cg-review pipeline into a goal-driven execution loop inspired by Codex Goals. The plan becomes a completion contract defining six properties: outcome (what should be true when done), verification surface (tests/benchmarks/artifacts that prove it), constraints (what must not regress), boundaries (allowed scope), iteration policy (how to choose next action), and blocked-stop condition (when to pause and report). /cg-work executes against this contract — validating inline, self-reviewing against criteria, and continuing until evidence confirms the outcome or a blocker is hit. Deviation policy is declared in the plan: 'ask' (pause for permission), 'autonomous' (deviate and report), or 'strict' (never deviate). A full implementation report is produced at completion showing: what was achieved vs. planned, any deviations with justification, evidence gathered, and remaining uncertainty. The separate /cg-review command remains available for adversarial/cross-model review but is no longer required as a default post-work step.

milestones.title: Knowledge Brain
milestones.objective: Build a concept-centric knowledge system that indexes all .cg-docs/ artifacts, organizes them by topics/themes with typed relationships, and enables cross-project knowledge sharing via a central team brain repository.

features.title: Full-scope indexer (all .cg-docs/ + roadmap features)
features.description: Extend cg_index.py to scan all .cg-docs/ subdirectories (solutions, plans, brainstorms, reviews, strategies) plus roadmap.json features as entities. Currently the indexer only covers .cg-docs/solutions/. The extended indexer must parse frontmatter from all artifact types and extract entity metadata (id, title, date, category, tags, status, related references). Roadmap features are ingested from the structured JSON directly. Output: a unified entity registry used by downstream features (topic extraction, relationship detection, BRAIN.md generation). Design inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki (https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f) and OmegaWiki (https://github.com/skyllwt/OmegaWiki). Batch A — develop together with brain-topic-extraction, brain-relationship-detection, brain-md-generation.

features.title: Topic/theme extraction (auto-cluster artifacts into concepts)
features.description: Auto-cluster indexed artifacts into topics/themes by analyzing tags, categories, and content overlap. Each topic gets a slug, one-line summary, and list of constituent artifacts across all entity types. Topics are the PRIMARY navigation layer in BRAIN.md — when an agent searches for knowledge, it finds topics first, then drills into specific artifacts. Example topics: 'PowerShell 5.1 compatibility', 'Pester safety', 'prompt design patterns'. Topics emerge from the data (tag frequency, category groupings, explicit references) rather than being manually defined. Batch A — develop together with brain-full-scope-indexer, brain-relationship-detection, brain-md-generation.

features.title: Relationship/edge detection (full typed edge set)
features.description: Parse explicit frontmatter links (related:, implements:, resolves:) and infer edges from content references between artifacts. Full edge type set from day one: implements (plan → feature), resolves (solution → plan finding), supersedes (newer → older artifact), decided_from (plan → brainstorm), reviews (review → plan), references (any → any general citation). Edges stored as structured data (source, target, edge_type) for use in BRAIN.md generation and future team brain push. Batch A — develop together with brain-full-scope-indexer, brain-topic-extraction, brain-md-generation.

features.title: BRAIN.md generation (topic index + entity catalog + edges)
features.description: Generate a single BRAIN.md file that serves as the agent's panoramic entry point to project knowledge. Structure: (1) Topic/theme index — primary navigation, each topic with constituent artifacts and key takeaways; (2) Entity catalog — secondary, organized by entity type (solutions, plans, brainstorms, reviews, strategies, features); (3) Edge list — relationship tracking showing how artifacts connect. Replaces current DIGEST.md as the canonical knowledge overview. Designed to fit in one context window (~100-300 entries) without requiring vector DB. Inspired by OmegaWiki's context_brief.md concept. Batch A — develop together with brain-full-scope-indexer, brain-topic-extraction, brain-relationship-detection.

features.title: /cg-brain-rebuild explicit rebuild command
features.description: Create a /cg-brain-rebuild command that explicitly triggers a full brain rebuild (re-runs the indexer, topic extraction, relationship detection, and BRAIN.md generation). This is the escape hatch for when the user wants an up-to-date brain without running /cg-compound. Batch B — develop together with brain-auto-rebuild-on-compound.

features.title: Auto-trigger brain rebuild on /cg-compound
features.description: Wire brain rebuild into the /cg-compound workflow so the brain stays current automatically. After a solution is captured and saved, the compound command triggers a full brain rebuild before completing. This ensures BRAIN.md always reflects the latest knowledge state. Batch B — develop together with brain-rebuild-command.

features.title: Prompt integration — Consult Brain in Step 0
features.description: Add a 'Consult Brain' sub-step to Step 0 of all major prompts: /cg-brainstorm, /cg-plan, /cg-work, /cg-review, /cg-fix-triage, /cg-compound. The agent reads BRAIN.md, identifies topics/entities relevant to the current task (by matching tags, categories, or feature references), then drills into specific artifact files for detailed context. This is the READ PATH that makes the brain useful — without it, the index exists but nothing consumes it. Each prompt uses the brain differently: /cg-brainstorm checks for prior explorations; /cg-plan checks for existing solutions to sub-tasks; /cg-work checks for gotchas; /cg-review checks for known mistakes; /cg-compound checks for superseded solutions. Batch C — develop together with brain-query-skill.

features.title: cg-skill-brain-query (agent brain search patterns)
features.description: Create a skill that teaches agents how to efficiently search and consume the project brain. Covers: how to scan BRAIN.md topic index for relevant clusters, when to drill into specific artifacts vs. trusting the summary, how to handle contradicting information (prefer newer, check supersedes edges), how to cite brain findings in outputs, and how to flag stale or potentially outdated knowledge. This skill is loaded by any prompt that has the 'Consult Brain' step. Batch C — develop together with brain-prompt-integration.

features.title: Team brain — central repo schema design
features.description: Design the GitHub repository structure for the cross-project team brain. This repo aggregates knowledge from all projects using the compound-gpid plugin. Key design decisions: how multiple projects' knowledge coexists (namespaced by project? flat merged?), what the team-level BRAIN.md looks like, how topic deduplication works across projects, and what metadata is needed for provenance tracking. Batch D (Phase 2) — develop first in team brain phase.

features.title: Team brain — push solutions + distilled patterns
features.description: On /cg-compound, after local brain rebuild, extract the solution plus auto-distill reusable patterns (project-agnostic lessons learned) and push to the central team brain repo. Only solutions and distilled patterns cross the project boundary — plans, brainstorms, and reviews stay project-local. The push mechanism must handle: authentication to the central repo, formatting entries for the team brain schema, and updating the team-level index. Batch D (Phase 2) — develop together with team-brain-pull.

features.title: Team brain — pull relevant entries during Step 0
features.description: During the 'Consult Brain' step in Step 0, after checking the local project brain, also fetch relevant entries from the team brain by matching topics/tags to the current task. This enables cross-project knowledge transfer — a solution found in project A becomes available to project B without anyone explicitly sharing it. The pull mechanism must handle: fetching from GitHub, caching locally for offline use, and relevance filtering (don't load the entire team brain into context). Batch D (Phase 2) — develop together with team-brain-push.

features.title: Team brain — conflict/dedup resolution
features.description: Handle contradicting solutions across projects. When two projects push solutions for the same topic that conflict, the system must resolve or flag the contradiction. Approaches: timestamp-based precedence (newer wins), confidence scoring based on how many projects validated the solution, or explicit 'contradicts' edges that surface both options with context. Batch D (Phase 2) — develop after push/pull are working.

features.title: Team brain — privacy filter before push
features.description: Ensure project-specific details (file paths, credentials, internal variable names, proprietary data references) are stripped or anonymized before pushing to the central team brain. The filter runs automatically during the push step. It should detect and redact: absolute paths, environment-specific configuration, internal API endpoints, team member names (unless opted in), and any content marked as sensitive in frontmatter. Batch D (Phase 2) — develop together with team-brain-dedup.

milestones.title: Ongoing Ideas
milestones.objective: Catch-all for standalone improvements and ideas that don't fit an existing milestone.

features.title: Command default behaviors (auto-branch, phases, autofix, context enrichment)
features.description: Establish opinionated defaults for the five main workflow commands so users get the most common behavior without flags. /cg-brainstorm: if the user is on the main or default branch, automatically create a new feature branch before starting (no prompt); if on any other branch, prompt the user whether to stay or create a new branch — branching is still the default unless overridden with a --no-branch flag. /cg-plan: default output is a phased plan (numbered phases with self-contained task lists) unless the user explicitly requests a flat plan via --no-phases. /cg-work: default is to run all plan phases sequentially (equivalent to current behavior without a phaseN argument); single-phase execution remains available via '/cg-work phase1'. /cg-review: default to autofix mode (automatically apply safe fixes from findings) rather than report-only; a --report-only flag disables autofix. /cg-compound: after capturing the solution, automatically add all key findings from the compound iteration to compound-gpid.context.md and any other relevant project files (skills, instructions), as long as they fit the project's structure and objectives — no manual prompting required.

features.title: Outcome criteria in plans (verifiable acceptance criteria)
features.description: When a user runs /cg-plan or /cg-brainstorm, the output must specify not only what to build (objectives, tasks) but also how the finished result should appear — concrete acceptance criteria that are verifiable during /cg-work and /cg-review. This includes: specific requirements the implementation must satisfy (e.g., 'function returns X when given Y'), observable behaviors or outputs (e.g., 'API responds with 200 and JSON schema Z'), structural constraints (e.g., 'no new dependencies added'), and measurable thresholds where applicable (e.g., 'test coverage above N%'). During /cg-work, the agent checks criteria as it completes each phase. During /cg-review, the agent explicitly verifies each criterion and reports pass/fail status. This closes the gap between 'plan says build X' and 'review can confirm X was built correctly'.

features.title: Conversation audit trail across workflow stages
features.description: Persist the main ideas from conversations between the user and compound-gpid throughout the entire workflow lifecycle: brainstorm, plan, work, review, and compound stages. The audit trail captures: the user's original request and how it was interpreted, clarifying questions asked by the agent and the user's answers, how the plan was adjusted based on those answers, decisions made during implementation (why approach A was chosen over B), review findings and how they were resolved, and any scope changes that occurred mid-session. This record is stored alongside the plan/brainstorm artifacts (not in a separate system) so that any future session can understand not just what was decided but why. Serves two purposes: (1) traceability — if a decision is questioned later, the reasoning is recoverable; (2) continuity — if a session is interrupted and resumed days later, the context is preserved without relying on the user's memory.

features.title: Attribution documentation (source repos and websites)
features.description: Create a dedicated documentation space (e.g., docs/attribution.md or CREDITS.md) that credits all repositories, websites, blog posts, and other resources used for researching and informing compound-gpid's design. This includes: the three competitive review repos (compound-engineering-plugin, superpowers, GSD-2), any additional repos the user provides, blog posts or articles that influenced prompt design patterns, documentation sources for tools and frameworks (Pester, PowerShell, GitHub Actions), and any community discussions or forum threads that contributed ideas. Each entry should include: the resource name/URL, what it contributed (specific pattern, idea, or validation), and when it was referenced. This serves both as professional attribution and as a reference index for future research sessions.

features.title: /cg-strategy --add <idea> quick-add mode for roadmap ideas
features.description: Add a --add flag to /cg-strategy that provides a streamlined path for capturing a single idea into the roadmap without running a full strategy session. When the user runs '/cg-strategy --add <idea text>', the flow is: (1) Parse the idea from the inline argument. (2) If the idea is vague or underspecified, ask targeted clarifying questions to develop it — what problem does it solve, who benefits, what does the finished result look like. (3) Once the agent has a clear understanding, explain the idea back to the user in its own words and ask for confirmation that it captured the intent correctly. (4) Suggest an existing milestone where the idea fits best, explaining why, or propose creating a new milestone if none fits. (5) On user approval, dispatch @cg-roadmap to add the feature with a detailed description (matching the level of detail in other Ongoing Ideas features). This bypasses the full strategy conversation (trigger selection, structured Q&A, proposal iteration) when the user already knows what they want — it's a fast lane for 'I have one idea, put it on the roadmap'. The full /cg-strategy flow remains available for sessions that need broader thinking.

features.title: Auto-generated project wiki (created at /cg-setup, updated at /cg-compound)
features.description: Create and continuously maintain a user-readable documentation wiki (similar to compound-gpid's own docs/ folder) that serves as the canonical reference for any project using the plugin — whether it's a research paper, R package, data pipeline, or tool. The wiki is initialized during /cg-setup based on the project charter, scanner results, and project type: for an R package it might include installation, API reference, and vignettes sections; for a research paper it might cover methodology, data sources, and replication instructions; for a tool it might cover setup, usage, and configuration. After initialization, /cg-compound automatically updates the wiki whenever a completed task produces knowledge that belongs in user-facing documentation — new features get documented, changed behaviors get updated, resolved bugs that affect usage get noted. The wiki is distinct from .cg-docs/ (which is internal compound-gpid knowledge) — this is external-facing documentation that end users and collaborators read. Flexibility mechanisms: the user can customize the wiki structure via a configuration section in compound-gpid.context.md (e.g., preferred sections, tone, audience), can run a dedicated command to restructure or regenerate specific sections, and can manually edit wiki pages without the plugin overwriting their changes (the plugin appends or proposes diffs, never force-overwrites). The wiki should also support a table of contents and cross-linking between pages.

features.title: Planning-stage test strategy + human review facilitation
features.description: During /cg-plan, explicitly define: (1) how the agent will test and validate the work (test commands, assertions, verification steps), and (2) how the human will independently review the result without needing /cg-review. The plan output includes a 'Verification' section that the human can follow post-implementation. Separates machine validation (automated, agent-run) from human validation (visual, logical, domain-specific).

features.title: Agent-verified outcome definitions with acceptance evals
features.description: During planning, define what 'done' looks like in concrete, verifiable terms. Reviewer agents then confirm outcomes were met — not just 'code works' but 'the outcome matches the stated definition.' Closes the loop between plan intent and review judgment. Complements outcome-criteria-in-plans (which defines what to check) with the verification mechanism (how to check it).

milestones.title: Token Optimization & Model Governance
milestones.objective: Reduce AI-credit cost and context burden by auditing token usage, defining model tiers with escalation rules, shrinking always-on context, splitting large prompts into thin entrypoints, adding stage-specific context contracts, and making review cheaper with deterministic pre-checks.

features.title: Audit current context and model usage
features.description: Measure the current token and AI-credit burden of Compound GPID. Covers prompt files, agent files, skills, instructions, shared files, documentation references, Knowledge Brain artifacts, and explicit model declarations. Produces: context/model audit script, context audit report, model-declaration inventory, list of largest context-cost sources, list of prompts/agents with missing or expensive model assignments.

features.title: Define model tiers and escalation rules
features.description: Create a model-governance policy defining when Compound GPID should use economy, standard, reasoning, or premium models. Premium models used only through explicit escalation conditions, not as ordinary defaults. Produces: model tier definitions, escalation rules, workflow-to-model guidance, updated model guidance documentation.

features.title: Add model-policy tests
features.description: Add automated checks preventing accidental expensive model usage, missing model declarations, or inconsistent prompt/agent model assignments. Produces: tests for model assignments, tests for premium model restrictions, warnings/failures when prompts or agents violate the model policy.

features.title: Update prompt frontmatter model and agent choices
features.description: Review all slash-command prompt files and assign appropriate model and agent defaults. Lightweight commands use economy or auto defaults. Planning, review, and debugging commands use stronger models only when justified. Produces: updated .github/prompts/*.prompt.md frontmatter, reduced expensive model usage in ordinary commands, clearer routing from prompts to agents.

features.title: Update custom agents for model and tool governance
features.description: Move model/tool governance into custom agents where appropriate. Agents define their intended role, tool access, model posture, and escalation behavior. Produces: updated .github/agents/*.agent.md, clear separation between lightweight/standard/deep-review/adversarial agents, restricted tool access for agents that don't need broad capabilities, premium agents gated behind explicit escalation.

features.title: Shrink always-on context
features.description: Reduce the size of instructions loaded automatically. The root Copilot instruction template should act as a short router, not a full manual. Produces: smaller .github/copilot-instructions.template.md, smaller instruction-router files, less repeated always-on text, clear pointers to stage-specific prompts/skills/context files.

features.title: Split large prompts into thin entrypoints and on-demand skills
features.description: Refactor large slash prompts so they act as workflow entrypoints rather than carrying all reusable doctrine. Move repeated or specialized guidance into skills and reference files loaded only when relevant. Produces: smaller prompt files, more focused skill landing pages, reusable doctrine in skill references, less duplication across prompts/agents/instructions.

features.title: Add stage-specific context contracts
features.description: Define exactly what each workflow stage should read, avoid, and produce. Prevents broad context loading and makes the workflow more interpretable. Produces: context-contract files for major stages, explicit read-first lists, explicit do-not-read-by-default lists, required output schemas for each stage, context expansion rules requiring stated reason before loading broader context.

features.title: Make review cheaper with deterministic checks first
features.description: Revise the review workflow so deterministic checks run before expensive LLM review. Use tests, linting, static checks, schema validation, and file-change classification before dispatching review agents. Produces: revised review workflow, cheaper first-pass review path, conditional escalation to specialist/premium review agents, reduced unnecessary multi-agent fan-out.

features.title: Benchmark before and after
features.description: Run comparable tasks before and after optimization to measure whether changes actually reduce context burden and model cost without degrading workflow quality. Produces: before/after benchmark report, estimated token burden by workflow, model usage comparison, quality notes from real Copilot runtime tests, list of remaining optimization candidates.

features.title: Capture the learning
features.description: After the optimization cycle is validated, capture the reusable lesson through the Compound GPID knowledge workflow. Produces: .cg-docs/solutions/ entry documenting the optimization pattern, updated Knowledge Brain artifacts, guidance for future prompt/agent/skill/model-governance changes.
